loading-screen-tips.page_modified_display: This page was last modified 04:07, April 19, 2022 (Update 53.1)
loading-screen-tips.scoped_visible_text: Tip #179: Most beneficial effects have a bonus type, such as enhancement, morale, or luck. Different types of bonuses stack, but usually the same types of bonus do not, with the exception of dodge bonuses, most circumstance bonuses, and racial bonuses.

fortification.page_modified_display: This page was last modified 10:54, October 24, 2026 (Update 82.0.1)
fortification.scoped_visible_text: Items are the primary source of fortification for most player characters. Standard fortification items provide enhancement bonuses to fortification. Multiple effects do not stack with each other. You can combine them with rarer Insightful Fortification items (insight bonus). Item effects fully stack with the racial fortification, enhancements, or epic destiny perks.

stack.page_modified_display: This page was last modified 16:01, December 12, 2025 (Update 77)
stack.scoped_visible_text:
Stacking follows a few predictable general rules:

Bonuses of the same type do not stack:
An enhancement bonus to AC from armor is an Armor bonus. The enhancement bonus to AC from a shield is a shield bonus. In this case, the two bonuses to AC do stack.
When an armor bonus to AC is granted by something other than armor or a docent (such as Black Widow Bracers), it does not stack with an actual armor.
When a Shield bonus to AC comes from something other than a shield (such as the Shield (spell)), it does not stack with an actual shield.
Untyped bonuses stack. Note that a bonus without a keyword isn't necessarily an untyped bonus, the description might just be lacking.
Penalties always stack.
Feat bonuses stack. A character with Lightning Reflexes (+2 bonus to Reflex saves) and Luck of Heroes (+1 bonus to all saves) will have a +3 Reflex save.
Bonuses from character Enhancements that don't mention a specific bonus almost always stack. They are not automatically "enhancement bonuses."
Note: Character enhancements with exactly the same name do not stack, other than the T3 & T4 Ability score enhancements.
Benefits from the same family, like Fortification or False Life, do not stack.
Damage Reduction does not stack (e.g. Stoneskin), except for the added DR that comes from active blocking (therefore it's not a waste to use it together with Barkskin which grants an increase to AC, i.e. an unrelated modifier).

enhancement.page_modified_display: This page was last modified 20:13, July 23, 2026 (Update 81)
enhancement.scoped_visible_text: An enhancement bonus represents a magical increase in the effectiveness of an item. Multiple enhancement bonuses of the same type do not stack. Also, enhancement bonuses that cover many areas do not stack with a specific type. For example, Speed which provides an enhancement bonus to move speed does not stack with Striding. Only the highest enhancement bonus applies for each type. Therefore, only an item or a spell is necessary to get the best bonus, so as you begin equipping items that provide bonuses like Acid Resistance, casting Resist Energy becomes unnecessary. Many types of Enhancement bonuses exist.

insight.page_modified_display: This page was last modified 12:15, June 18, 2026 (Update 80)
insight.scoped_visible_text:
An insight bonus improves performance of a given activity by granting the character an almost precognitive knowledge of what might occur. Multiple insight bonuses do not stack, only the highest applies.

Generally, item enchantments that grant an Insight bonus to a particular stat have a value equal to half that of an equivalent level enchantment giving an Enhancement or Equipment bonus to the same stat, rounding down.

quality.page_modified_display: This page was last modified 11:16, July 27, 2017 (Update 36.1)
quality.scoped_visible_text: A quality bonus makes a character better at an action through sheer good workmanship of the item in question. Like most bonus types, multiple quality bonuses do not stack, only the greatest bonus applies.

profane.page_modified_display: This page was last modified 06:16, January 7, 2025 (Update 71.1)
profane.scoped_visible_text:
A profane bonus (or penalty) stems from the power of evil. Multiple profane bonuses on the same character or object do not stack. Only the highest profane bonus applies.

Some of the most common sources of profane bonuses include:

Several named item sets
Lunar Gems
Profane Well Rounded items
Profane Spell Focus Mastery items

festive.page_modified_display: This page was last modified 20:35, February 29, 2016 (Update 30)
festive.scoped_visible_text:
When the Festive bonus was originally introduced in Update 28 Patch 1 it was known as a Spooky bonus. It was renamed in Update 30 to support being used on non-scary things.

Some of the reward items from The Night Revels special event grant this unique bonus. Multiple effects with the same bonus type don't stack, only the highest applies.

reviewed_interpretation.int: The affirmative Tip 179 clause supports exactly ten unordered selected-gear Intelligence pairs among Enhancement, Insight, Quality, Profane and Festive. It is not the converse of same-type nonstacking. Each selected component remains independently qualified; same-type suppression, Artifact and Exceptional rules remain separate.
reviewed_interpretation.scope_limit: No universal all-stat/all-type default. No adoption of adjacent loading tips, historical dodge/circumstance/racial exceptions, or new character/DPS/crit conclusions. The rule page was last modified in 2022 despite its 2026 observation.
reviewed_interpretation.stack_caveat: The Stack article's general same-family bullet is retained, not hidden. Reading it as banning every differently typed bonus to one stat conflicts with the specific Fortification Enhancement/Insight combination. No INT-specific contrary exception was established in this bounded review; this is not exhaustive absence proof.
reviewed_interpretation.fortification: The fresh standard-item/Insightful paragraph supports the existing Enhancement/Insight interaction prospectively. It does not classify the selected Chains Prefix, qualify Queen, or establish complete Fortification.
reviewed_interpretation.spot: Current Skills +20 recipe magnitude is supported, but the two older Five Rings images do not qualify current Chains Spot +20. No Spot mixed-type rule is introduced.
